meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste the time. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. So what is the zero based on, Hale?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
Show me the page. A misquoted line is a mistake in an essay, Hale, so is that the whole basis for the zero?
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.
"It seems to run in the family." I'm writing that down, Hale, and you'll want to be very careful about your next sentence, because the principal will be hearing it.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You told me in the meeting that you should have called me before entering the zero, and that you are sorry. I still require the zero withdrawn from Owen's English 30-1 essay. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: at her opening position with nothing agreed, still wanting the zero withdrawn and still intending to go to the principal.
What moved her: "I should have called you before entering the zero" got her only a flat okay, because you owned the process in one sentence and moved on.
What cost ground: "It seems to run in the family" cost the most, because it brought up Claire and Owen's character together and turned her cold.
Try next time: when she asked to see the page with the quoted line, put the dated document in front of her so she could check it herself, and leave her family out of it.
